questions.question: What does the AWS shared-responsibility model mean for an application team?
options: AWS operates defined cloud infrastructure while the customer still owns workload identity, data, configuration, architecture, and use
AWS owns every application security decision
The customer owns physical data-center security
Managed services require no operational testing
questions.explanation: Responsibility changes by service, but customer architecture and configuration obligations do not disappear.

questions.question: Why can an evenly distributed three-AZ fleet still fail during one AZ loss?
options: Even placement does not guarantee the remaining two zones have enough reserved capacity for peak demand
Availability Zones share every power system
Load balancers cannot use zones
Autoscaling removes all warm-up time
questions.explanation: Failure reserve must be sized explicitly after removing the largest failed placement slice.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a backup and failover capacity?
options: A backup preserves recoverable data; failover also needs a healthy serving target, routing, capacity, and a promotion procedure
Backups always have zero RPO
Failover never uses replicas
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Durability evidence alone does not establish live availability or recovery time.

questions.question: When should a workload use an IAM role instead of a long-lived access key?
options: Whenever the runtime can obtain short-lived scoped credentials
Only for root users
Only in one Availability Zone
Never for managed services
questions.explanation: Short-lived role credentials reduce secret distribution and support scoped, auditable authorization.

questions.question: Why must architects classify data-transfer paths?
options: Internet, cross-AZ, cross-region, NAT, and service paths can have different latency, resilience, and cost behavior
All network bytes have identical behavior
Transfer never affects architecture
Only DNS traffic is metered
questions.explanation: Topology determines both failure coupling and transfer economics.

questions.question: What should a multi-region failover test prove?
options: Routing, standby capacity, state promotion, dependency endpoints, reconciliation, and safe failback
Only that a second Region exists
Only that backups are enabled
Only that DNS records can be edited manually
questions.explanation: A regional recovery path crosses many independent control and data-plane contracts.

questions.question: Which service-selection question should come before choosing a named AWS product?
options: What access, consistency, scaling, failure, security, and operational contract does the workload require?
Which service has the longest feature list?
Which console page appears first?
Which logo is most familiar?
questions.explanation: Requirements should select the primitive, then current service capabilities should be validated.

questions.question: Which signal makes cloud cost actionable?
options: Spend attributed to an owner, workload, environment, unit of demand, and outcome
One unsegmented monthly total
Instance count without utilization
A list of all service names
questions.explanation: Unit economics and ownership connect resource usage to an engineering decision.
